correctness.rationale: Use the published minimal-order classification as input. The units are 1+J because the residue field is F₂. The square-zero elementary abelian central subgroup 1+Z₀ has order eight; independent cosets of J/Z₀ have unit commutator 1+w because their ring commutator annihilates J. The resulting nondegenerate alternating form proves that this subgroup is the full unit-group center. In central coordinates the square map is xu+yv+xyw. Modulo w it is linear: rank zero gives the two binary Arf types, rank one is split by the square (0 or w) of its unique nonzero kernel vector, and rank two has one orbit. Changing quotient and center bases gives precisely the presentation equivalence. The square-zero cosets give 8|q^{-1}(0)| elements including the identity, and the Frattini space is spanned by u,v,w. The resulting signatures distinguish the five groups; in the first and third types the generators with w give D₈ and Q₈ with the other two central factors splitting off. Independently read and transcribed Tables 1–3 and Props. 4.1–4.3 rather than running the frozen checker. In characteristic four the shifts to the ring square pair are zero for 2·1 in W₀, (s₁,s₂) in Prop. 4.2, and (w,0) in Prop. 4.3. The seven independent count rows in frozen order are (2,4,1,3,0), (1,2,1,2,3), (2,4,1,3,0), (3,6,1,6,0), (1,2,1,2,3), (2,4,1,3,0), and (2,6,1,7,8). They give the exact characteristic split and totals. This checks the transport of the published representatives, not the completeness proof for rings independently.

value.rationale: The unit group is a natural multiplicative invariant of these extremal rings. A complete distribution with presentations and an inexpensive intrinsic type signature explains how the 88 ring classes collapse under this invariant, including the effect of changing characteristic. This exact structural census can be used without reconstructing radical multiplications every time.
